# Ahmadreza Samadi

> I build AI, and I run a business that has to live with it.

Ahmadreza Samadi, also known as Ahmad Samadi, is a Dubai-based technology entrepreneur. As Co-Founder & Technical Lead of Appraiva, Samadi builds AI products. As Co-Founder & CEO, he runs Royal Abraj Group. He writes about how businesses decide what to build, check and measure.

## Profile

- [Homepage](https://a-samadi.com/): Ahmadreza Samadi builds AI and runs a business that has to live with it. Explore his work at Appraiva, Royal Abraj Group in Dubai and his decision guides.
- [Biography](https://a-samadi.com/about.html): Biography of Ahmadreza Samadi, also known as Ahmad Samadi. Follow his path from data engineering to building AI products and running a business in Dubai.
- [Ahmadreza Samadi press kit, biography and founder roles](https://a-samadi.com/press.html): Find Ahmadreza Samadi’s short and long biographies, portrait and official profiles. Check his Dubai base and his current roles at Appraiva and Royal Abraj Group.
- [Where AI belongs in a business](https://a-samadi.com/ideas.html): Three questions to ask before using AI in a business. Which decision will it improve, who will check the result, and what does each accepted result cost?
- [Now](https://a-samadi.com/now.html): What Ahmadreza Samadi is working on in November 2026: building AI at Appraiva, running Royal Abraj Group, and a weekly piece on where AI earns its place in business.
- [Writing topics](https://a-samadi.com/speaking.html): Writing topics from Ahmadreza Samadi's work in AI products, property data and business systems, with related published work and written contact details.

## Work

- [AI Products and Business Systems](https://a-samadi.com/work/): Explore Ahmadreza Samadi’s work on property imagery and search at Appraiva, customer workflows at Royal Abraj Group, and data engineering at Oxfam Novib.
- [Appraiva case study: property imagery, data and search](https://a-samadi.com/work/appraiva.html): How does Appraiva match a property photo to the right record? Ahmadreza Samadi explains how imagery analysis, matching and data enrichment support investor search.
- [Royal Abraj Group in Dubai and Ahmadreza Samadi’s role](https://a-samadi.com/work/royal-abraj.html): Follow how Ahmadreza Samadi connects an enquiry to CRM follow-up and a customer portal at Royal Abraj Group, a Dubai brokerage and documents-clearing business.
- [Oxfam Novib: CRM data and analytics](https://a-samadi.com/work/oxfam-novib.html): Ahmadreza Samadi’s Oxfam Novib work: Azure data infrastructure for CRM migration and analytics as a Data Engineer, September 2022–June 2023.
- [Hamrah e Aval (MCI)](https://a-samadi.com/work/mci.html): Ahmadreza Samadi’s MCI work used RFM and behavioral data for customer segmentation, churn-risk analysis and campaign targeting, without uplift claims.

## Tools

- [Before You Build the AI](https://a-samadi.com/tools/before-you-build-ai.html): Turn an AI idea into a decision, an evidence plan and a small first experiment. A free interactive field guide by Ahmadreza Samadi.
- [Rental cash flow calculator](https://a-samadi.com/tools/rental-cash-flow.html): Separate annual rent, property costs, debt cash payments and upfront invested cash using your own AED inputs. Blank values remain unknown.
- [Dubai property purchase costs and buyer fee calculator](https://a-samadi.com/tools/dubai-purchase-cost.html): Estimate the fees a buyer pays on a completed residential property in Dubai. Enter your quotes and payer shares to see how much each cost adds to the purchase.
- [Valuation range checker](https://a-samadi.com/tools/valuation-range.html): Compare two to five property estimates: median, range, spread and transparent review flags. Your inputs stay in your browser.
- [Dubai rental yield calculator for gross and net income](https://a-samadi.com/tools/dubai-rental-yield.html): Calculate gross and net rental yield for a Dubai property using your own rent, vacancy and expenses. See how service charges change the income you keep.

## Writing

- [Writing on AI products and business](https://a-samadi.com/writing/): Read Ahmadreza Samadi on building AI products, testing them on real tasks and counting review costs. Explore property examples and everyday technology explainers.
- [Start with the decision, then build the AI](https://a-samadi.com/writing/start-with-the-decision.html): A practical approach to AI product decisions: start with the customer’s decision, assess the evidence, and evaluate the whole workflow.
- [AI evaluations: test the task, not just the demo](https://a-samadi.com/writing/business-ai-evaluation-cases.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains why a polished AI demonstration does not establish reliability for the real task: choose evaluation cases from the work.
- [AI cost per accepted result](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-cost-per-verified-result.html): A practical framework for measuring AI workflow cost: include tokens, tools, retries and human review, then divide by results that pass verification.
- [AI in real estate decisions: where AI should stop](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-human-review-real-estate.html): AI can prepare real estate information; people must verify material claims and explain uncertainty before a client decides. Use an explicit review handoff.
- [AI agent safety policy for accounts, tools and approvals](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-agent-safety-boundaries.html): Define which accounts, data and tools an AI agent can access. See where permissions are enforced, when a person approves an action and how to revoke access.
- [How to check an AI home value estimate against sales](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-home-value-estimates.html): When two AI estimates disagree on a home's value, start with the facts each used. Review the sale dates, comparable homes and uncertainty before relying on a figure.
- [Dubai property costs and data: choose the right source](https://a-samadi.com/writing/which-dubai-property-source.html): Choose Dubai property sources by purpose: sale and mortgage fees, rental benchmarks, sales-price indices or a specific valuation. Keep dates and limits visible.
- [AVM vs. appraisal when comparable sales are limited](https://a-samadi.com/writing/avm-vs-appraisal.html): Compare an automated valuation, a broker opinion and an appraisal. See how missing sales, uncertain property condition and the intended use affect the choice.
- [How does property data enrichment connect the right records?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/property-data-enrichment.html): A fictional image-and-record comparison shows how to check property identity, source dates and unresolved claims before combining property information.
- [I build AI, and I run a business that has to live with it](https://a-samadi.com/writing/build-ai-run-a-business.html): Ahmadreza Samadi builds AI at Appraiva and runs Royal Abraj Group in Dubai. Three questions for deciding where AI belongs in a business, and where it must stop.
- [Connecting apps to AI: account access and approvals](https://a-samadi.com/writing/connected-ai-apps.html): What can a connected AI app read or change? Use examples from ChatGPT and Gemini to check the account, the scope of access and the actions that require approval.
- [What the Jev AI decision model does in a business workflow](https://a-samadi.com/writing/jev-ai-decision-model.html): See how TypeSafe describes Jev, how it picks from a bounded set of outcomes and what you need to check before a model's decision can route a business task.
- [Passkey vs. Face ID: what a website actually receives](https://a-samadi.com/writing/passkeys-face-id.html): Face ID unlocks a passkey locally. Follow a sign-in to see how the site checks the cryptographic proof, where your face data stays and how recovery fits in.
- [How ZIP files compress data and restore every byte](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-zip-files-work.html): See how lossless ZIP compression stores repeating data and rebuilds the original file. Find out why a folder of photos or videos may shrink very little.
- [How to verify an image and the claim attached to it](https://a-samadi.com/writing/verify-ai-image-claims.html): Trace a photo back to its source, try a reverse image search and compare independent evidence. Learn what provenance can tell you when a photo is called AI-made.
- [Do foldable phones have two batteries and one charge level?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/foldable-two-batteries.html): See how two batteries power a folding phone with one charge indicator. Different cell capacities explain why averaging the two percentages can mislead you.
- [Humanoid robots at home: what can they do on their own?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/humanoid-robots-at-home.html): What does a humanoid robot shipment tell you about its ability to work at home? Compare deliveries, demonstrations and evidence of autonomous household tasks.
- [How satellite messaging works when your phone has no signal](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-satellite-messaging-works.html): Trace a phone message through a satellite to a ground station. See why delivery can take longer than a regular text and how sky visibility affects the connection.
- [What Incognito mode hides and who can see your browsing](https://a-samadi.com/writing/incognito-private-browsing.html): When you close an Incognito window, what disappears from your device? Follow a gift purchase through browser history, cookies, saved files and website records.
- [Why AI sounds confident when wrong](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-ai-sounds-confident.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains confident AI mistakes with a fictional museum example, an animated film and a simple way to check claims against evidence.
- [What does Accept cookies actually mean?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/what-accept-cookies-means.html): The same small browser note can remember your shopping basket or help a company recognise you across websites. The choice is about what that note does.
- [Why your phone stops charging at 80% and what to check](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-phone-stops-charging-at-80.html): A phone can pause at 80% because of a charge limit, its learned routine or heat. Check the setting and the conditions around the pause to tell the causes apart.
- [How can a profitable business run out of cash?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/profitable-but-out-of-cash.html): A profitable sale can leave a business unable to pay its supplier. Follow one order to see why earned money and available cash are different.
- [Why can 8% rental yield still leave a cash shortfall?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-rental-yield-cash-flow.html): A correct rental-yield calculation can still leave a cash shortfall. Follow a fictional home from headline yield to money left after costs and the loan.
- [Does full storage slow down a computer with free RAM?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-full-storage-slows-computer.html): See why a nearly full drive leaves less room for temporary files, memory overflow and SSD housekeeping. These examples explain when freeing space can help.
- [iPhone Duo vs. iPhone 18 Pro: the price gap per day](https://a-samadi.com/writing/iphone-duo-price-per-day.html): Compare the $800 US launch-price gap by day of ownership. Check the installment example and see how an uncertain resale value affects the cost calculation.
- [How contactless cards work without a battery inside](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-contactless-cards-work.html): Trace a contactless payment from the reader's radio field to the card's chip. See how a tap supplies power and carries payment data back to the terminal.
- [How noise cancellation works](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-noise-cancellation-works.html): Microphones measure outside noise and a speaker adds a carefully timed opposite wave. Why this reduces a hum better than every sudden voice.
- [Why USB-C cables with the same plug charge differently](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-usb-c-cables-differ.html): Two USB-C cables can look alike and support different charging power, data speeds or video. Check what the cable, charger and device support before choosing one.
- [How phones read text in photos](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-photo-text-recognition-works.html): OCR finds text regions and recognises visual patterns as letters and words. The AI feature can save typing, but copied text still needs checking.
- [Why Wi-Fi can be slow even when you have full bars](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-wifi-is-slow-with-full-bars.html): Full Wi-Fi bars measure signal strength between your device and router. Compare local congestion, the internet connection and the service to locate the slowdown.
- [Why AI forgets earlier messages in a long conversation](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-ai-loses-earlier-chat-context.html): Your chat history can contain details the model no longer sees. Compare the context window, summaries and saved memory to understand why a chatbot misses a detail.
- [How many coffees must a café sell to break even each day?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-many-coffees-to-break-even.html): A fictional café sells 100 coffees for $500 and earns no operating profit. Follow the price, variable cost per cup and fixed costs to calculate its break-even point.
- [How a digital twin models a real building](https://a-samadi.com/writing/how-building-digital-twins-work.html): Sensors connect real rooms and equipment to an updating digital model. See how a building digital twin turns readings into useful context.
- [How ChatGPT’s intelligent UI turns answers into tools](https://a-samadi.com/writing/chatgpt-intelligent-ui-explained.html): Explore ChatGPT's interactive answers using a fictional budget. Changing a number shows what the interface can calculate and which assumptions still need checking.
- [How do property tokens work, and can you sell them?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/dubai-property-tokenisation-explained.html): A simple property-token explainer connects digital ownership, fractional shares and net rent with the separate challenge of finding a buyer.
- [Choosing a smaller AI model](https://a-samadi.com/writing/small-ai-models-task-routing-explained.html): Haiku 5.5 is a current example of narrow AI work. Learn task definition, evaluation, routing and a fictional cost calculation without assuming equal quality.
- [AI data-center site readiness](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-data-center-site-readiness.html): Power, cooling, networks and building fit explained through fictional sites, with current JLL and Meta sources and questions for specialist review.
- [Why does moving data matter for AI chips?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-inference-memory-movement-explained.html): Our original framework: identify the workload, locate the bottleneck, then test the complete result. No chip test, measured saving or vendor ranking is claimed.
- [Building laser scans explained](https://a-samadi.com/writing/building-laser-scans-point-clouds-explained.html): Use a scan as evidence for a defined question. It does not certify structural safety, hidden services or universal accuracy. No real building was scanned.
- [Why does AI need weather stations?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-ai-weather-models-need-local-observations.html): AI weather models need current observations as well as past patterns. Check location, update time and forecast window, and distinguish radar from forecasts.
- [Why rent divided by home value is not property yield](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-rent-to-value-is-not-property-yield.html): Why a metro rent-to-value ratio is not an observed property yield. A fictional cash budget shows the difference and the next evidence to check.
- [Why did the lights go out while you were there?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/why-occupancy-sensor-lights-switch-off.html): Why occupancy sensors can miss a seated person: check their view, movement detection and timeout before asking the facilities team to investigate.
- [How a virtual PC can use your real printer](https://a-samadi.com/writing/virtual-machine-device-sharing-explained.html): Our original checklist: Which virtual PC? Which resources? Do I need each one? The film is conceptual, not product footage or a tested setup.
- [Who checks the AI’s homework?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-document-review-claim-evidence-checklist.html): A document-review checklist by Ahmadreza Samadi: write the claim, locate its supporting evidence, then resolve the gap or keep it visible.
- [Your building sent an alert.](https://a-samadi.com/writing/building-leak-alert-response-checklist.html): A fictional building leak alert shows why a named responder, a location check and a recorded outcome matter. Three questions to ask before buying a sensor.
- [Where does your wearable’s AI run?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/where-wearable-ai-computation-runs.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains wearable AI computation: which tasks run locally, what data is sent out and what happens without a connection.
- [The message looks convincing.](https://a-samadi.com/writing/on-device-ai-scam-warnings-explained.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains AI scam warnings: stop a rushed action, verify through a trusted separate contact route and keep uncertainty visible.
- [Your thermostat speaks. Who listens?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/bacnet-building-devices-common-language.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains BACnet building integration: identify the devices, data and commands, and who verifies that they work together.
- [A map answer. The right place?](https://a-samadi.com/writing/geospatial-ai-map-answer-review.html): Ahmadreza Samadi’s geospatial AI checklist: check the boundary, date, source and assumptions behind a map answer; keep unsupported conclusions open.
- [Why your phone puts you across the street](https://a-samadi.com/writing/phone-location-across-street.html): A fictional pickup explains reflected satellite signals, an uncertain map dot and a practical way to agree where to meet.
- [AI agents need shared notes, and a way to check them](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-agents-shared-notebook.html): A fictional repair workshop explains reusable agent knowledge, context checks and a boundary for private project information.
- [Tesla says Roadster can fly: three questions to ask](https://a-samadi.com/writing/tesla-roadster-flight-claim.html): Ahmadreza Samadi’s fictional hangar explains thrust and separates a manufacturer’s Tesla Roadster claim from availability and public-road approval.
- [Rent or buy: the five numbers that decide it](https://a-samadi.com/writing/rent-or-buy-five-numbers.html): Compare rent and ownership using matched housing, running costs, upfront cash, time and net exit proceeds. Keep cash affordability separate from wealth.
- [Where the person signs off: property AI review](https://a-samadi.com/writing/human-review-property-ai-checklist.html): A practical human-review checklist for property AI: define the decision, check evidence, preserve uncertainty and record who can approve the next action.
- [Dubai property buying costs, item by item](https://a-samadi.com/writing/dubai-property-buying-costs.html): Build a dated Dubai purchase budget from official registration fees, mortgage charges and your own quotes. Separate total fees from the buyer’s share.
- [How cold outdoor air can help warm a home](https://a-samadi.com/writing/heat-pump-moves-heat-explained.html): Ahmadreza Samadi explains how a heat pump moves heat through a fictional home and an illustrative energy balance, with an English animated film.
- [AI agents: ability is not authority](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-agent-permissions-ability-authority.html): Ahmadreza Samadi uses a fictional invoice to explain business AI permissions: the boundaries between reading, drafting and approving an action.
- [Dubai service charge: same rent](https://a-samadi.com/writing/dubai-service-charge-same-rent.html): A fictional Dubai comparison by Ahmadreza Samadi separates advertised rent from cash after service charges, with DLD’s definition and limits.
- [RAG: check the record behind an AI answer](https://a-samadi.com/writing/rag-check-business-records.html): In a fictional hotel, Leila asks an AI assistant for a meeting-room quote. Before sending its fluent answer, she checks the source and finds an old price list.
- [Dubai project escrow: control is not a guarantee](https://a-samadi.com/writing/dubai-project-escrow-controls.html): Fictional buyer Rami sees a model of an unfinished building and asks which records support its payment instructions. No real project or account is represented.
- [AI computer use: check the result, not just the click](https://a-samadi.com/writing/computer-agent-check-result.html): In a fictional parcel studio, Nora asks an AI helper for a label. A panel moves before the click arrives: the cursor moves, but the label is still missing.
- [Property comparables: evidence beyond the nearby price](https://a-samadi.com/writing/property-comparables-evidence.html): Fictional buyer Mina compares neighbouring flats: one asking price and one older agreed sale. Nearby doors do not make them identical valuation evidence.
- [Building digital twins: ask how fresh the data is](https://a-samadi.com/writing/building-digital-twin-data-freshness.html): In a fictional office, Omar sees a polished building model while a room feels wrong. Check which physical asset the data describes and when it was observed.
- [Prompt injection: give documents less power](https://a-samadi.com/writing/prompt-injection-layered-controls.html): A fictional theatre shows why a document should not control an AI assistant. Fewer tools, content checks and human approval can limit misleading instructions.
- [AI research output needs examination and understanding](https://a-samadi.com/writing/ai-research-examination-understanding.html): Zara reviews an AI-generated research result. Follow her questions about the evidence, assumptions and limitations behind a polished answer in this fictional case.
- [Cash conversion cycle: follow the three clocks](https://a-samadi.com/writing/cash-conversion-cycle-clocks.html): Follow a fictional lamp workshop from buying inventory to collecting cash. See why a recorded sale and cash available to pay a bill can fall on different days.
- [Structured AI output: correct shape is not truth](https://a-samadi.com/writing/structured-output-source-checks.html): Follow Noor as she checks a delivery date against a supplier quote. A fictional example shows how an AI response can fit its schema and still get a fact wrong.
- [Building energy audits: diagnose before replacing](https://a-samadi.com/writing/building-energy-audit-decisions.html): A fictional building manager investigates a high energy bill. Follow the audit questions about equipment and daily operation before deciding what to replace.
- [More AI agents can expose a shared bottleneck](https://a-samadi.com/writing/agent-workflow-shared-bottlenecks.html): In a fictional dispatch library, every helper needs the same key. Follow the queue to see which tasks an extra agent can take on and which still have to wait.

## Topics

- [Business AI and operations in Dubai](https://a-samadi.com/topics/business-systems-dubai.html): Follow a customer enquiry at Royal Abraj Group in Dubai, then explore how to assess an AI assistant’s access, review steps and cost per accepted result.
- [AI in real estate: evidence and decisions](https://a-samadi.com/topics/ai-real-estate.html): A reading path through property data, human review, AI workflow costs and rental cash flow, with Ahmadreza Samadi’s work at Appraiva as context.
- [Tech, explained](https://a-samadi.com/topics/tech-explained.html): Plain-language technology explainers and original films. Choose a mechanism, check its limits, and connect it to the decision you need to make.

## Studies

- [Property Decision Data](https://a-samadi.com/studies/): Open property studies by Ahmadreza Samadi, with source years, geography, assumptions, methods and practical decision tools.
- [Rent vs owning: 393 metro cash-budget scenarios](https://a-samadi.com/studies/rent-own-2026/): Rent vs owning through hypothetical landlord cash budgets across 393 metros. Compare HUD rent areas, ACS values, costs and limits; not a personal buy-or-rent answer.
- [Rent burden in 386 US metros: ACS 2024](https://a-samadi.com/studies/rent-burden/): A reproducible ACS 2024 study of 30% and 50% gross-rent-to-income thresholds, with explicit denominator exclusions and uncertainty limits.
- [Property studies explorer](https://a-samadi.com/studies/explorer.html): Search US metro rent-burden estimates and illustrative ownership budgets. Keep data years, assumptions and geography limits visible.

## Explainers

- [AI agents are learning when to ask.](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-assisted-permissions.html): GitHub has made assisted permissions generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code. The useful question is what still needs your approval.
- [Technology explainers](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/): Source-dated visual explainers by Ahmadreza Samadi on AI and business technology, with the original slides, source links and companion pages.
- [AI usage and useful business outcomes](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-ai-usage-not-outcomes.html): GitHub has expanded Copilot usage reporting across tools. That helps show activity. It does not measure business results by itself.
- [What a Gemini business hub can do](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-gemini-business-hub.html): Google announced a Gemini landing page for small businesses, with brand, finance and connected-app tools. Start with the workflow you need.
- [An AI factory needs more than GPUs.](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-ai-factory-observability.html): NVIDIA announced Minerva, an AIOps platform connecting infrastructure and workload signals. The trend is visibility across the whole operation.
- [World models and real-world tests](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-world-models-real-tests.html): NVIDIA expanded Cosmos with data, training and simulation tools for physical AI. Generated scenarios can broaden what developers test.
- [A chat request is not a shipped fix.](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/tech-trend-notification-to-reviewed-fix.html): GitHub announced a consolidated Teams app that connects issue notifications with Copilot. The review step still belongs in the workflow.
- [How to check a Dubai broker record](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/dubai-broker-record-check.html): Follow a Dubai broker record check through the official listing. See which details identify the broker and which property and transaction facts need separate checks.
- [Dubai project status and registration](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/dubai-project-status-check.html): Match a Dubai project to its registered record before reading a progress update. Use the slides to check that the evidence describes the same project.
- [Dubai rental index and asking rents](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/dubai-rental-index-context.html): Compare a Dubai asking rent with an official rental index result. Keep the property details, advertised price and index evidence distinct as you read each slide.
- [Dubai procedure status: check the actual result](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/dubai-procedure-status-check.html): Read a Dubai procedure status in context. Follow the slides to distinguish what the record currently shows from the outcome someone expects to happen next.
- [Dubai valuation: identify the evidence behind the number](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/dubai-valuation-evidence.html): Compare property valuation evidence in Dubai. Identify the type of value, its source and the purpose of the comparison before relying on a figure for a decision.
- [AI property briefs: keep claims tied to evidence](https://a-samadi.com/carousels/ai-property-brief-evidence.html): Review an AI-generated property brief slide by slide. Trace each important claim to its source, identify missing evidence and decide what still needs checking.

# Appraiva: turning property imagery into decision support

At Appraiva I build AI that connects property photos with records, and at Royal Abraj Group I run a business where people decide how to act on an AI answer.

By Ahmadreza Samadi · Co-Founder & Technical Lead

## Decision: connect an image to property research

An image can show the condition of a property. Turning that observation into useful investment research takes more than an AI model.

Ahmadreza Samadi has been Appraiva’s Co-Founder & Technical Lead since October 2023 and works remotely from Dubai for the US company in Cleveland, Ohio. It builds AI tools that help real estate investors and developers find distressed and off-market properties through imagery analysis and enriched property data.

For property research, a condition signal needs context: which property it describes, what other information is available, and how a person can find and use it. Those questions connect model output with product design and engineering.

Samadi describes his approach: “I build AI, and I run a business that has to live with it.”

## Responsibilities: connect imagery, data and search

Ahmadreza Samadi’s responsibilities connect imagery analysis, property matching, data enrichment, search, AI and cloud architecture. The work spans four connected areas:

• Property discovery: connect imagery analysis to the property it describes.

• Data enrichment: bring condition signals together with other property information.

• Search: make that information available within an investor's research workflow.

• Product and infrastructure: connect the interface, data systems, AI workflows and cloud services that support those steps.

The architectural challenge is keeping those connections useful: an image observation needs a property identity, supporting context and a clear next step in the product.

## Current role and scope

Ahmadreza Samadi’s current role at Appraiva is Co-Founder & Technical Lead. The company combines imagery analysis and enriched property data to help real estate investors and developers find distressed and off-market properties.

The research example below is fictional; this page does not report investment returns or current customer-adoption results.

## What does property data enrichment add to an image?

Property data can provide context for an image: which property it describes, when the information was recorded and what still needs to be checked. Appraiva’s founder announcement is an existing public reference for the company.

## How does an observation become useful research?

A reviewer needs to know which property an observation describes and what other information supports it. Linking imagery, records and search is one way to make that context available within a research workflow.

The next step depends on the evidence. An image and a property record may describe different moments. Connecting them is useful only when a person can understand the context and identify what still needs investigation.

## Which questions help decide what to investigate next?

For illustration, consider a fictional research record: an image appears to show wear on a roof, while the property record is incomplete. These suggested questions would help decide what to investigate next:

• Is it the correct property? Check that the image and supporting records refer to the same property before combining their information.

• How current is the evidence? Compare image-capture and record dates; distinguish a past observation from information about present condition.

• What is observed, and what remains unresolved? Separate what appears in the image from claims that still need records or professional verification.

• What information is needed next? Identify the missing fact and appropriate follow-up before turning research into a recommendation.

For checks on property facts and uncertainty, see what AI home-value estimates miss. Where AI should stop in real estate explains preparation, verification and the client’s decision. AI cost per accepted result includes review effort in a proposed workflow evaluation.

## Explore the product approach

Samadi explains this approach in Start with the decision, then build the AI. To apply the questions to your own idea, use the Before You Build the AI field guide.

## Public reference

Appraiva’s founder and launch announcement, 12 January 2024, identifies Ahmadreza Samadi as Co-Founder & Lead Data Architect and describes the platform’s early beta at that time. The historical title and beta reference belong to January 2024; his current title is Co-Founder & Technical Lead.

# Ahmadreza Samadi at Royal Abraj Group

By Ahmadreza Samadi · Co-Founder & CEO · Dubai, UAE

## Decision: give each system a clear purpose

A customer enquiry is the beginning of a workflow. The business still needs to understand the request, follow up, manage the work and keep the customer informed.

Ahmadreza Samadi has been Co-Founder & CEO of Royal Abraj Group in Dubai since 2022. The group covers property brokerage and documents-clearing services. He leads its digital strategy and technology.

Samadi’s system responsibilities cover websites, CRM workflows, a customer portal and internal tools. The work connects enquiry capture and sales follow-up with document handling, case tracking and customer information.

These boundaries matter because a sales record and an active customer case answer different questions. Someone following up on an enquiry needs the next sales action. Someone delivering a service needs the current work, the responsible person and the information required to proceed.

## Responsibilities: separate sales follow-up from service delivery

Samadi’s digital work covers the following system responsibilities:

• Website: explain the service and capture the enquiry.

• CRM: organize lead information and the next sales follow-up.

• Customer portal: support document handling and visibility into customer work.

• Internal tools: connect case information, delivery status and team responsibilities.

A lead’s next sales action and a case’s next delivery action need to remain clear as work passes between people and systems.

For teams considering AI access to these kinds of business systems, Samadi’s article Connected AI apps: access, scope and approval explains how to distinguish reading information from taking action. Use the decision worksheet to map who should check a proposed assistant’s next step.

## Current role and scope

Samadi’s contribution connects the customer-facing website and portal with CRM workflows and internal operations.

This case study describes supported system responsibilities; it does not report a measured sales or efficiency result.

## Professional background and contact

For Samadi’s current roles and broader experience, visit his biography or his LinkedIn profile. The Royal Abraj Group website provides information about the business and its services.

The Royal Abraj Properties leadership page provides public company context.

For a property decision, start with the Dubai property source guide to distinguish an index, a rental benchmark and a valuation service.

## Company update: comparing brokerage quotes

Reviewed 27 October 2026

Royal Abraj Group announced a seven-point brokerage-fee checklist and a free two-quote worksheet in Royal Abraj Properties’ English and Persian buying-cost guide. The worksheet records fee scope, payer, VAT, included services, separate costs and payment terms; it does not set a commission rate or replace an agreement.

Essay · Start with the decision

# Start with the decision, then build the AI

An AI product earns its place when it helps someone make a useful decision and act on it. Define the evidence, responsible person and acceptance rule before choosing a model, then test the complete workflow.

## Key points

• Name the decision and the responsible person first.

• Define acceptable evidence, missing-data behavior and human review.

• Test the full workflow against a recorded baseline.

Original editorial comparison — all amounts and cases are fictional

Step

Value or evidence

Interpretation

Decision

Which fictional records need investigation?

A named researcher chooses the shortlist

Evidence

## A decision brief before a model brief

Define the decision, evidence, responsible person and acceptance rule before choosing the AI system. A useful experiment tests the whole path from evidence to action.

Decision

Evidence and review

Action and measurement

Work backward from one decision, then test the complete workflow.

For the hypothetical property shortlist in this essay, write the brief as: “A researcher chooses which records deserve further investigation, using dated evidence with unresolved fields visible.” Compare that process with the current manual approach. A shortlist is a research aid; it is not a purchase recommendation or a verified finding about a property.

### A checklist for the next experiment

• Name one decision and the person responsible for it.

• Record the current process, including its cost and failure cases.

• Define acceptable evidence and what happens when it is missing.

• Set the acceptance rule and the human review point before testing.

• Compare the same task under both workflows; retain rejected cases and review effort.

Use the decision brief or tool · Explore the three signature ideas

### Primary references

• Google: Rules of Machine Learning

• NIST AI RMF 1.0

• Microsoft Research: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction

These references inform the evaluation and interaction principles. The workflow above is an editorial synthesis, not an endorsed standard or a reported company outcome.

When I assess an AI product idea, I start with a business question: what decision is difficult today, and what would make it easier?

That question provides a practical starting point for both product strategy and engineering. It identifies who needs the result, what information matters, and what the system must do beyond producing an answer.

## Which decision should this AI product help someone make?

Consider a hypothetical property research tool. “Analyze properties with AI” leaves many product choices unresolved. “Help an investor decide which properties deserve further investigation” is more specific. It identifies an action and a point in a workflow where better information could help.

The distinction matters because a useful research tool may need to show supporting evidence, make comparisons easy, and identify missing information. A single score would only cover part of that job.

## What evidence would make the decision responsible?

Once the decision is clear, ask what evidence a person would need to make it responsibly. In this example, that might include imagery, its capture date, relevant property attributes, and the limits of what can be inferred.

Then ask whether the necessary data is available, sufficiently current, and appropriate for the use case. These questions belong early in product development because the answers can change what the product should promise.

## What action follows the answer?

An output becomes useful when it fits the next step. Does the customer shortlist an opportunity, request additional information, or send a case for human review?

That action shapes the interface and the architecture. It determines which information must be retained, which integrations matter, and where a person needs to be able to question or correct the system.

## How would I evaluate the whole workflow?

For this hypothetical tool, I would evaluate several questions together:

• Does it surface information that is relevant to the research decision?

• Can a user understand the evidence and its limitations?

• How much review is needed before taking the next step?

• What happens when information is incomplete or the system is wrong?

• Is the value of that assistance worth the cost of delivering it?

A model metric can inform those questions, but it cannot answer all of them. Product evaluation also needs to examine the experience of the person using the result.

## What is the smallest useful commitment?

I would rather define an initial product around one decision we can support well than make a broad promise that is difficult to evaluate. A focused scope gives the team a clearer way to learn from customers and decide what to build next.

My approach is to connect the customer’s decision, the supporting evidence, the product workflow, and the engineering effort. That connection is where technical capability becomes a business proposition.

## Put the method to work

Before You Build the AI turns these questions into an interactive decision brief. Explore a worked example, adapt it to a product idea, and export a first experiment.

For the professional context behind my interest in property research workflows, see my work on AI real estate intelligence at Appraiva. The example in this essay remains hypothetical.

01—03

## A smaller promise. A clearer test.

Illustrative example loaded. Change any detail, then rebuild your brief.

### 01 / The decision

A property researcher Which properties deserve a closer investigation before an investor commits more time? How ready is that evidence? Some is available; gaps remain If the answer is wrong… It creates meaningful rework or cost Who reviews before action? A person reviews every result

### The next action

Shortlist candidates and request missing information or a manual inspection.

### 02 / The evidence

Dated property imagery, relevant property attributes and source provenance. Record what the imagery cannot establish.

### Resolve first

Make the gaps visible. Identify missing sources and define when the tool must ask for information or hand the decision back to a person. Keep the reviewer in the test. Record corrections and the time needed to review each result, alongside the model output.

### 03 / The smallest useful experiment

• Choose a small, explicitly scoped set of cases for this decision. Include typical cases, missing evidence and plausible failures. Do not treat a small pilot as proof of broad reliability.

• Establish the baseline: A researcher checks each listing and builds a shortlist manually. Record time, outcomes and correction effort.

• Prepare evidence-backed suggestions for the same cases, manually or with a simple prototype. Keep the reviewer in the test. Record corrections and the time needed to review each result, alongside the model output.

• Compare against your criterion: Reduce research time while retaining useful candidates, with missing evidence visible and review effort included. Set measurable pass and stop conditions before testing; include delivery and review costs.

### Proceed only when

The evidence supports the intended action, failures have a clear fallback, and the combined workflow improves on the baseline. If it does not, narrow the decision or revisit the inputs.

A structured thinking aid, not an AI assessment or a readiness score. Guidance follows your selections; it does not validate the evidence.

# Where AI belongs in a business

Three questions to ask before using AI in a business. Which decision will it improve, who will check the result, and what does each accepted result cost?

These are the principles I use to explain and design AI workflows. They are supported by the linked essays and tools, rather than claims of measured company results.

## Start with the decision.

Name the decision, the person making it and the evidence it needs before choosing a model.

### Why it matters

A model is a component. A useful product also needs a person, evidence, a next action and a way to judge whether the decision improved. Starting there makes the limits visible before an experiment grows.

• Name the decision

• Identify the evidence

• Choose the next action

• Then test the AI

A decision workflow for start with the decision.

### Where I apply it

• Read the decision-first field guide

• Write a decision brief

• Explore explicit ownership scenarios

• How I decide where AI belongs in a business

### Use it tomorrow

• Write one decision as a question a person needs to answer.

• Name the person responsible for the next action.

• List the evidence and what would make it insufficient.

• Choose an acceptance rule before comparing tools.

## Where the AI must stop.

Make the point for human checking, override or sign-off part of the product.

### Why it matters

An answer and an action carry different consequences. Property identity, missing information, permissions and accountability need explicit checks. A person must be able to see the evidence and stop or override the proposed action.

• AI proposes

• Check source and limits

• Person accepts or overrides

• Authorized action

A decision workflow for where the ai must stop.

### Where I apply it

• Read about human review in real estate

• Set an agent’s permissions

• Check the property identity and source

### Use it tomorrow

• Identify the error that could affect the decision.

• Put the human check before that consequence.

• Show source, date and uncertainty at the check.

• Specify what happens when evidence or approval is missing.

## Cost per accepted result.

Include retries, failures and review when counting the cost of a result that meets an explicit acceptance rule.

### Why it matters

A cheaper request may require more retries or review. Count the full workflow cost against distinct results that meet an explicit acceptance rule. The cost ledger records caller acceptance; it does not independently certify the output.

• All attempt costs

• Include tools and review

• Count accepted results

• Divide cost by results

A decision workflow for cost per accepted result.

### Where I apply it

• Read the workflow-cost essay

• Use the cost ledger and fictional worked examples

• Set an acceptance rule

### Use it tomorrow

• Define what counts as one distinct result.

• Write the acceptance rule and who applies it.

• Record failed attempts, retries, tool costs and review time.

• Report no accepted results as undefined cost per result, not zero.

Analysis · AI product economics

# AI cost per accepted result

Divide the full recorded workflow cost, including failed attempts, retries, tools and human review, by distinct results accepted under a rule fixed before the test. With no accepted results, unit cost is undefined. This is a measurement method, not independent certification of the outputs.

## Key points

• Include all recorded attempts, retries, tools and review costs.

• Count distinct accepted results under a fixed rule.

• With zero accepted results, unit cost is undefined.

Fictional costs, not a measured benchmark

By Ahmadreza Samadi · 24 September 2026 · Updated 21 October 2026

## Measure cost per accepted result

Divide all recorded workflow costs by the number of distinct results accepted under a rule fixed before the test. Include retries and rejected attempts in cost; do not count repeated attempts as new accepted results.

All attempt costs

Acceptance rule

Cost per accepted result

Total recorded cost ÷ distinct accepted results. With none accepted, unit cost is undefined.

This guide uses “accepted result” for an output that meets the complete acceptance rule recorded before the test. “Verified result” in the historical URL and earlier title refers to that same rule; neither term establishes independent certification. Keep unknown costs separate from explicit zero. Compare the same intended result batch and currency, and report acceptance counts alongside unit cost. A lower unit cost with a weaker acceptance rule is not a like-for-like improvement.

### A checklist for the next experiment

• Freeze the task, intended result IDs and acceptance rule.

• Record model, tool, labor and other costs consistently for all attempts.

• Retain rejected attempts and retries in the numerator.

• Count each accepted result once; report unknown cost inputs as unknown.

• If no result is accepted, report total spend and zero accepted results, with unit cost undefined.

## How can I try this with my own ledger?

The offline ledger records costs and acceptance labels supplied by the user; it does not independently verify outputs. The teaching fixture has three attempts, two intended results, one accepted result and a total cost of 0.85. All amounts are fictional. Missing costs are rejected; explicit zero remains zero. Use the same task, currency and acceptance rule for both workflows.

## How do you calculate cost per accepted result?

I would start with a simple measure:

Cost per accepted result = total workflow cost ÷ distinct results meeting the declared acceptance rule.

The numerator includes model input and output, cached context, tool calls, retries, failed runs, and human review time. The denominator counts outputs that meet a defined standard for the task. A low price per request can still produce an expensive result when many requests fail or need extensive correction.

If no output meets the acceptance rule, report the experiment’s total spend and zero accepted outputs separately. Cost per accepted result is undefined for that run; do not report it as zero or infinity.

Compare workflows only for the same defined task and acceptance criterion, and include the relevant cost categories consistently. Read cost per accepted result alongside precision, recall and time to a decision; a lower cost figure alone does not show that the workflow is more useful.

This is a measurement framework, not a universal benchmark. Teams need to define what “accepted” means for their own workflow and record the assumptions behind any cost comparison.

## Does passing review mean the work is accepted?

Define the full acceptance rule before the test. Passing review may be the entire rule, or only one requirement. If the rule also requires use in a stated destination, delivering a file or passing review alone does not fulfill it.

Fictional example: spend 15 currency units across three intended results. Two pass review, but only one is also used in the stated destination. If acceptance requires both checks, count one accepted result: 15 / 1 = 15. Dividing by two gives 15 / 2 = 7.50 per review-passed result, a different denominator rather than evidence of improvement.

Record who will use the output, where it must be used, which checks and rework come first, and who records acceptance. The ledger calculates the labels you supply; it does not independently verify quality, use or business outcomes.

Read the published acceptance guidance (English)

Before recording a run, complete the blank experiment notes (in English), or read the filled fictional notes (in English). Identify the intended user, destination and acceptance evidence, and record checking and rework under your stated rule. The filled notes explain the original fictional fixture only; they supply no actual output evaluation or destination test.

## How does this connect to my work?

I am Co-Founder & Technical Lead of Appraiva, a US company in Cleveland, Ohio, and work remotely from Dubai. Appraiva builds AI tools that help real estate investors and developers find distressed and off-market properties through imagery analysis and enriched property data. The property-research test in this article is a proposed experiment, not a description of an Appraiva feature or a reported company result.

## How would you test a property-research workflow?

Imagine testing a tool that flags property records for further investigation. Start with a human-labeled set of records. Ask the system to surface candidates with supporting evidence. Have a reviewer accept or reject each suggestion, then measure precision, recall, total cost, and time to a decision.

That is a proposed experiment, not a description of an Appraiva feature or a reported company result. It illustrates why a model that is cheaper to call might still cost more per accepted candidate if it sends too many false leads to a reviewer.

### What would I test first?

• Choose one repetitive task and write down the current human process.

• Define a clear acceptance rule before running the AI test.

• Track model, tool, retry and review costs for every attempt.

• Compare accepted results and time to decision against the current process.

The useful question is whether the workflow helps someone reach a reliable decision at a cost that makes sense. Lower model prices make that test easier to run; they do not answer it by themselves.

Essay · Building and operating

# I build AI, and I run a business that has to live with it

By Ahmadreza Samadi · 9 November 2026

I do two jobs that look at AI from opposite sides. At Appraiva, I build it. At Royal Abraj Group in Dubai, I run a business that has to live with what it does. Each job keeps the other honest.

## The builder’s side: the model is the smaller part

At Appraiva, a US company in Cleveland, Ohio, I’m Co-Founder & Technical Lead, working remotely from Dubai. We build AI tools that help real estate investors and developers find distressed and off-market properties through imagery analysis and enriched property data.

Building taught me that the model is the smaller part of the product. An image can suggest a worn roof. Before that observation helps anyone, it has to be matched to the right property, set beside dated records and shown where a person can decide what to check next. Most of the engineering lives in those connections, not in the model.

So the builder’s question is practical: what does a person need around the model’s output before they can act on it?

## Where the two sides meet: three questions

Building and operating push me to the same three questions before I choose a model:

• Which decision should this improve? “Use AI for customer service” is not a decision. “Help a customer see their next step on their own request” is.

• Where must a person check? Anything that changes a record, judges eligibility, quotes a price or commits money needs a named person and a visible route to them.

• What does an accepted result really cost? Count the reviews, the retries, the answers people reject and the limits you set, not just the price of a model call. I call this cost per accepted result.

The builder in me wants the model to do more. The operator in me asks who answers for it when it is wrong. The useful product usually sits where both are satisfied. Start with the decision, then build the AI works through the first question in detail.

## What I would tell another business owner

• Start smaller than the demo. One decision, one place, a small group of users who know it is new.

• Let ordinary software answer what has a known answer. It is cheaper, testable and does not improvise.

• Keep the model away from the keys. Reading and suggesting is one risk; changing records is another.

• Decide in advance who checks, and make the route to that person visible to the customer.

• Measure what was accepted, not what was generated.

AI is worth it where it shortens the path to a decision that a person still owns. It must stop where a wrong answer becomes a commitment.

## Why I write about it

Most writing about AI comes from people who sell it or people who study it. I write from the place where it is built and then has to work inside a real business, with real customers and a team that answers for it. That is the question I keep returning to at a-samadi.com: where does AI earn its place in a business, and where must it stop?

More: Appraiva case study · Royal Abraj Group case study · AI and business systems: lessons from Dubai

# How to check an image claim, AI-made or not

A convincing picture is not proof of its origin—or of the story attached to it. Check the claim around the image before trusting the pixels.

By Ahmadreza Samadi · 3 October 2026

Updated 14 October 2026

## At a glance

Check the image’s original context, date and publisher; search for earlier appearances; inspect provenance when available; and corroborate the caption’s important claim. An authentic file can still carry a false story, and missing provenance does not settle whether an image is AI-made.

## Why can’t appearance alone verify an image claim?

For my recent carousel, I made three realistic example photographs with AI and asked readers which one was generated. The answer was all three. The examples are demonstrations, not documentary images. Small oddities can prompt a closer look, but no visual clue reliably identifies every AI-generated image. The opposite mistake is just as important: a genuine photograph can appear with a false caption.

## Which four steps help check the claim?

• Find the original context. Look for the earliest credible post, its date, the publisher and what it actually claimed. A crop or repost may remove vital context.

• Search with the image. Google's image-search tools can surface related appearances. An older use with a different caption can reveal recycling, although a search with no match proves little.

• Inspect provenance when available. Content Credentials and other origin signals can show how supported media was created or edited. OpenAI notes that metadata can disappear after resizing, screenshots or re-uploads. Missing credentials are not proof that an image is authentic or AI-made; even detection tools have limits.

• Corroborate the important claim. Seek independent reporting, other photographs or video, official records, or a direct source that supports what the caption says. The more consequential the claim, the stronger this check should be.

The goal is not to win a game of spotting imperfect hands or strange shadows. It is to establish whether the event, person, place or statement in the caption is supported by evidence. An authentic file and an accurate story are different questions.

## What does a valid Content Credential establish?

The C2PA explainer separates verification of a file’s signed provenance from verification of its story. A valid credential can help check that the recorded history is associated with that file and has not been tampered with. It does not independently establish that the pictured event or the caption’s claims are true. Provenance may also be incomplete.

## How would I apply this to a property image?

Consider a hypothetical listing photo. Before using it as current property evidence, I would separate three claims:

• Identity: Can the original source and independent property information connect the pictured building to the stated property?

• Timing: Can the capture date be corroborated? A recent repost is not necessarily a recent photograph.

• Condition: Which visible conditions does the image support, and what remains outside its view or may have changed since capture?

If a claim cannot be corroborated, mark it unresolved rather than treating the image as current evidence for it. A provenance record can help trace the file; it does not complete these property checks. This is an illustrative review framework, not a reported Appraiva result or a verification of a real listing.

## See the original demonstration

The Instagram carousel and LinkedIn document show the three explicitly AI-generated example photos and the short verification workflow.

## Sources

• C2PA: Content Credentials, provenance limits and factual accuracy

• OpenAI: Advancing content provenance for a safer, more transparent AI ecosystem

• Google Search Help: Search with an image

# Two batteries, one foldable phone: how the battery reading works

A foldable phone can use two batteries to fit around its hinge while showing one charge reading. That reading estimates usable energy across the system; averaging the two percentages can mislead.

Continue reading: Tech, explained · Signature ideas

By Ahmadreza Samadi · 3 October 2026

Updated 19 October 2026

## At a glance

A combined battery reading estimates usable energy across the system. Capacity, load, temperature and health can matter, so simply averaging two percentages can mislead. The worked numbers below are illustrative; one icon does not reveal the device’s wiring or balancing algorithm.

## Why split the battery?

A folding hinge interrupts the space that an ordinary flat phone can use. Apple says its announced iPhone Duo places one high-energy battery on each side and uses Apple silicon and “energy rebalancing algorithms” to make them operate seamlessly as one. That confirms the two-battery design and the stated software-level goal. The announcement does not publish a detailed circuit diagram or the exact control algorithm, so the explanation below is about the general principle, not a teardown of iPhone Duo.

## How does one reading combine two stores of energy?

The phone needs to estimate how much usable energy remains in the system. Battery fuel gauges do more than read an instantaneous voltage: they estimate state of charge and health using models that can account for capacity, load, resistance and temperature. The phone can then present a single system-level reading while managing charging and power use behind the scenes. The exact physical connection and balancing strategy depend on the product design.

Why not just average the two displayed percentages? Suppose an illustrative battery A can store 12 watt-hours and is half full, while battery B can store 8 watt-hours and is full. In this example, 50% means half the energy stored when the battery is fully charged; a real phone’s displayed charge percentage may be calculated differently. They hold about 6 + 8 = 14 watt-hours out of 20, or 70% of their combined nominal energy. Averaging 50% and 100% would say 75% and overstate the total. These are made-up numbers, not iPhone Duo specifications. Real remaining-runtime estimates also depend on load, battery health and what part of the stored energy is usable.

## What can’t one battery icon tell you?

One icon makes the device easier to use, but it does not reveal each pack’s capacity, charge level or health. Nor does it prove the two packs are wired in series, in parallel or through a particular converter. Those details require product-specific documentation or a reliable teardown. The clear distinction is this: Apple confirms two batteries and energy rebalancing; the capacity-weighted example explains why a combined reading needs more thought than averaging two percentages.

My Instagram carousel and LinkedIn document post show the hinge constraint and the illustrative percentage example as short visual walkthroughs.

# Oxfam Novib: a data foundation for CRM and analytics

Azure data infrastructure for CRM migration and analytics.

Data Engineer at Oxfam Novib, September 2022–June 2023, building Azure data infrastructure for CRM migration and analytics.

By Ahmadreza Samadi

## Background: CRM migration and analytics

Ahmadreza Samadi builds AI products at Appraiva and runs Royal Abraj Group in Dubai. He writes about how businesses decide what to build, check and measure. My background includes Azure data infrastructure for CRM migration and analytics at Oxfam Novib.

## Professional context

My professional background includes enterprise data engineering and machine learning. The workflow notes below explain general data concepts.

## General workflow concepts

A data workflow can distinguish data arrival, transformation and downstream use. These stages provide a way to discuss preparation and analytical needs.

## Separating the stages of data preparation

Bronze, Silver and Gold are labels for stages of data preparation. As a general illustration, they can separate ingestion, transformation and downstream use; this is not a description of the Oxfam Novib implementation.

Questions about sensitive data, retention and operating documentation belong in planning a data workflow. Any specific implementation needs its own requirements and review.
